title: Air Operations Expert
description:
Job Overview

The Air Operations Expert will support the implementation of rulemaking, safety promotion and research activities under the European Plan for Aviation Safety (EPAS). In this role, the post-holder will contribute to the development of effective, proportionate and forward-looking air operations standards, working closely with internal and external stakeholders across the European and international aviation system.

The position requires the ability to lead complex technical activities and facilitate stakeholder discussions. It is suited to a professional with strong technical expertise and the ability to work independently on assigned tasks within a structured rulemaking environment.

Main Accountabilities

- Lead or contribute to assigned rulemaking, safety promotion and research tasks within areas of expertise, in line with the European Plan for Aviation Safety (EPAS).

- Develop and draft regulatory material, guidance material, acceptable means of compliance, and other relevant non-binding products related to air operations standards.

- Apply the Agency’s rulemaking procedures and contribute to the continuous improvement of methods, processes and ways of working.

- Act as a focal point for assigned technical domains within air operations standards, providing expert input and ensuring consistency of technical and regulatory positions.

- Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, including the European Commission services, to support the development, consultation, communication and implementation of regulatory outputs.

- Lead or support expert groups, stakeholder discussions, public consultations, workshops and meetings, including the preparation, conduct and follow-up of such activities.

- Prepare briefing notes, reports, analyses, presentations and other material to support decision-making, communication and stakeholder engagement.

- Represent the Agency, as appropriate, in meetings, workshops, conferences and other relevant fora.

- Monitor operational, safety, technological and regulatory developments, assess their potential impact, and contribute to the evolution of the regulatory framework.

- Contribute to the planning, monitoring and delivery of assigned tasks and outputs, ensuring alignment with milestones, quality standards and project objectives.

- Contribute, where relevant, to tender specifications, the evaluation of bids, and the oversight of externally contracted research and study projects.

- Support collaboration within the team, including providing back-up to peer Air Operations Experts during absences and key events.

Admission Criteria

The following constitute eligibility and essential criteria for the role and for being admitted to the selection process. Candidates not fulfilling these criteria by the deadline for applications, will be excluded from the selection:

- Have a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the European Union (at least level C1) and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the EU to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties (at least level B2). One of the required languages shall be English*.

- Be a national of a Member State of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland.

- Have completed university studies of at least three (3) years attested by a diploma in relevant subjects in scope of the profile.

- After obtaining the university degree, have at least two (2) years of professional experience acquired in relevant areas.

- Demonstrate professional experience in air operations regulation, oversight, standardisation, safety management or safety analysis.

- Have a proven track record in drafting, reviewing or implementing technical or regulatory aviation material.

The following constitute advantageous criteria for the role. Candidates not fulfilling these criteria will not be excluded from the selection process:

- Being or having been a qualified air operations inspector and/or RAMP inspector within an aviation authority.

- Familiarity with chairing or facilitating technical working groups involving multiple stakeholders.

- Familiarity with research, innovation or emerging technologies, safety risk management, safety analysis or operational risk assessment.

* English oral and written skills will be assessed throughout the assessment phase. Further language assessment may be organised, where necessary, to verify compliance with the requirement to demonstrate knowledge of two EU languages.

This vacancy is open as well to Temporary Agents (2f) employed at EASA, in the grade bracket AD5-AD9.

Selection Criteria

The selection process is based on the assessment of the Professional Skills and Behavioural Competences listed below. While these are considered critical to perform the role effectively, candidates who do not meet all criteria may still be considered.

Professional Skills

Rules Development Process

Basic Regulation

English Drafting of Technical Documents

ICAO Annex 6 - Operation Of Aircraft

Air Operations

EU Air Operations Regulations

Behavioural Competences

Flexibility & Change Adaptability

Professional & Technical Expertise

Communication

Teamwork

Critical Thinking

Mandatory Pre-Employment Requirements

Prior to recruitment, you will be requested to demonstrate that you:

- Are entitled to the full rights as a citizen

- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service

- Meet the character requirements for the duties involved (you will be asked to provide a police certificate confirming the absence of any criminal record)

- Are physically fit to perform the duties linked to the post (you will be asked to undergo a medical examination in a centre indicated by EASA)

Conditions of employment

Contract: 5 years contract as Temporary Agent 2 (f) with possibility of extension
Working hours: 40 hrs per week (on a full-time working pattern). Flexible working arrangements
Salary: Step in grade upon recruitment based on years of work experience. Additional allowances depending on personal situation
Location: Cologne, Germany (relocation is required)

title: Human Factors Expert
description:
Job overview

In the respective domain, ensure product safety and environmental compatibility by providing expert knowledge to influence decisions in certification and continued airworthiness, contributing to the safe integration of innovative and more sustainable technologies.

General accountabilities

In the respective domain:

- Provide expert advice and contribution to complex certification for the determination of the applicable certification basis, the definition of the level of involvement by selecting compliance demonstration items and the agreement of applicants’ certification programmes.

- Verify the compliance demonstrations provided by applicants for the domain of expertise in cooperation with the certification teams and experts of other technical domains.

- Develop and contribute to the definition of interpretative material and special conditions as well as assess requests for deviations or for equivalent level of safety to address new technologies, unconventional uses, and proposals for novel compliance demonstration.

- Ensure investigation of in-service occurrences and defects in the domain of expertise and contribute to the agreement of adequate corrective actions to maintain acceptable safety standards as well as to ensure follow-up of those actions wherever necessary.

- For the domain of expertise provide advice in the development of new airworthiness and environmental protection requirements, industrial standards, including relevant parts of EASA Certification Specifications and advisory- as well as guidance material.

- Provide inputs and support to Design Organisation Approval activities as necessary.

- Provide technical inputs to support the other Agency’s activities such as Research projects or Innovation Partnership Contracts

- Represent the Agency externally in international working-groups or standardisation bodies when requested to do so.

Admission criteria

The following constitute eligibility and essential criteria for the role and for being admitted to the selection process. Candidates not fulfilling these criteria by the deadline for applications, will be excluded from the selection:

- Have a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the European Union (at least level C1) and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the EU to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties (at least level B2). One of the required languages shall be English[1].

- Be a national of a Member State of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland.

- Completed university studies of at least 3 years attested by a diploma in Human Factors (e.g. social sciences, psychology, philosophy, sociology, linguistics, or cognitive/physical ergonomics, etc.), or in other relevant subjects in the scope of the profile (e.g. aeronautical engineering, aerospace engineering, automotive engineering, mechanical engineering, etc.),

- At least 3 years of relevant professional experience acquired in positions corresponding to the nature of the duties (defined under the general accountabilities part), obtained after the award of university diploma*.

- Proven professional experience in the field of human factors applied to aviation or comparable domain (e.g. automotive industry) with a specific focus on usability studies, human centred design or evaluation of Human Machine Interfaces.

* This vacancy is open as well to Temporary Agents (2f) employed at EASA, in the grade bracket AD5 - AD9

The following constitute advantageous criteria for the role. Candidates not fulfilling these criteria will not be excluded from the selection:

- Knowledge of the certification specifications and related material in the field of human factors applied to aviation.

- Knowledge of the aviation organisations and industry operating within the scope of the job description.

[1] Mother tongue English speakers will be expected to demonstrate knowledge of a second EU language. English oral and written skills will be assessed throughout the assessment phase.

Selection criteria

The selection process is based on the assessment of the professional skills and behavioural competences listed below. While these are considered critical to perform the role effectively, candidates who do not meet all criteria may still be considered.

Professional skills

EASA Regulations & Aviation Safety Standards

Human Factors

Human Factors Usability Studies

Human Machine Interface & Cockpit Integration

Certification Processes, Methods, & Specifications

Behavioural competences

Learning Agility

Teamwork

Critical Thinking

Professional & Technical Expertise

Stakeholder Orientation

title: Study Placement Scheme
description:
Job Overview

Through the SPS, you will acquire first-hand technical and operational experience by means of contact made in the course of your everyday work in the Agency and will further put into practice the technical knowledge you are gaining during your studies. Your accountabilities will depend on the needs of the Agency and on your profile (i.e. educational background and skills). You will be deployed in professionally enriching projects under the supervision of a study placement advisor and you will be involved in the day-to-day activities of your team.In addition to the on-the-job training, general and technical in-house training may be offered -if necessary- to support your tasks and learning objectives.

Eligibility and Selection criteria

To be admitted to the selection process you must meet the following criteria:

- In the context of your studies at University or equivalent institution, or as part of your professional qualification, need to complete a compulsory placement or write a final thesis.

- Be national of one of the EASA Member States or of a country with observer status in the EASA Management Board [1]. In exceptional cases and when in the interest of the service, nationals of other third countries may be considered.

- Have a very good knowledge of English and preferably of another language of the European Union [2].

The area of interest you indicate when submitting your application will be considered in assessing the relevant competencies required to align your profile with potential roles and units. While we strive to match candidates with suitable opportunities, the final assignment will be based on organizational needs and available positions.

[1] For the list of the EASA Member States and of the States represented by the EASA Management Board Observers, click here

[2] Mother tongue English speakers will be expected to demonstrate knowledge of a second EU language. English oral and written skills will be assessed throughout the assessment phase.

Behavioural competences

Communication

Teamwork

Learning Agility

Planning & Organising Skills

Conditions

Duration of the placement: Min. 6 weeks – max 6 months, as per mutual agreement between the student and the Agency

Location: Cologne, Germany

Weekly hours: 40

Financial contribution: N/A. All expenses incurred during the study placement are to be covered by the student. No financial support is granted by the Agency.

Accident and health insurance: EASA does not provide accident nor health insurance. Prior to the start date, students must provide proof that they are covered by sickness and health insurance as well as insured against accident risks for the entire duration of their stay at the Agency.

Selection Process & How to apply

Selection Process

The selection process is carried out in accordance with the EDD 2004-004. It encompasses the following steps:

Your application will be assessed against the eligibility criteria and required skills. If shortlisted, you will be contacted for an interview regarding your suitability and expectations. Only candidates interviewed will be notified of the outcome; those not selected will remain in the database for other opportunities until year-end.
If offered a position, you must provide required documentation, including proof of identity and education, health insurance, criminal record checks, and visa (if applicable).

How to apply

When applying, please ensure that you select your areas of interest in your candidate profile via the EASA Careers Portal. Please choose them by order, your preferred area of interests under "Interests area 1" and so on. This information will help us guiding our evaluation process and help match you with the most relevant opportunities. However, if your skills align with other open positions, you may also be considered for additional roles beyond your chosen areas of interest. We can only accept applications that are submitted in English through our Recruiting tool. Before sending your application, make sure it is complete and contains the document(s) specified in the vacancy notice. IMPORTANT: Before submitting your application, ensure that your candidate profile, all the fields and answers to the pre-screening questions are correct. In case of questions or technical issues, email us at recruit@easa.europa.eu. Attach a description and screenshot of the error.
